excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that individual users and relatively small teams will not become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights. This will likely require:
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendation is that developers argue individuals/small teams won't gain significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard and the ASL-3 Security Standard, which protect against misuse and model-weight theft by non-state adversaries, are required.

locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
excerpt: Restrictions on model behavior, and/or measures for quickly detecting and acting on Usage Policy violations, accompanied by a strong case that these measures are difficult to reliably, sustainably circumvent via jailbreaking.
paraphrase: Recommended measures include behavioral restrictions or violation-detection, backed by an argument these are hard to jailbreak around.

locator: Table 1 / Non-novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
excerpt: Precautions against opportunistic theft of model weights, such as centralized controls on third-party applications and software updates.
paraphrase: Recommended measures include precautions against opportunistic weight theft, such as centralized controls on third-party apps and updates.

excerpt: This column summarizes commitments drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts. It should be read as an overview, not as indicating any separate or additional plans.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Capability or usage threshold
excerpt: AI systems with the ability to significantly help threat actors (for example, moderately resourced expert-backed teams) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with potential for catastrophic damages far beyond those of past catastrophes such as COVID-19.
paraphrase: This row defines the threshold as AI substantially helping moderately resourced expert teams create weapons causing damage far exceeding COVID-19.
stated_bar: damages far beyond those of past catastrophes such as COVID-19
prior_counterpart_excerpt: CBRN-4: The ability to substantially uplift CBRN development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs (with relevant expert teams), such as by novel weapons design, substantially accelerating existing processes, or dramatic reduction in technical barriers.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company
excerpt: We will apply protections at least as strong as our ASL-3 protections (see previous row) to an expanded set of potential use cases for AI, covering the most likely vectors for this threat.
paraphrase: Anthropic will extend ASL-3-level protections to a broader set of use cases covering likely threat vectors.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: We expect this threshold will require the ASL-4 Deployment and Security Standards. We plan to add more information about what those entail in a future update.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-our plan as a company

excerpt: Additionally, we will identify the most concerning specific threat pathways, create policy recommendations for early detection and response for such threats, and share this content with policymakers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will identify key threat pathways, create early-detection policy recommendations, and share these with policymakers.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that threat actors will not become significantly more likely to cause the sort of catastrophic harm discussed in the lefthand column via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: The recommendation is that developers argue threat actors won't gain significantly increased ability to cause the described catastrophic harm.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: We expect this threshold will require the ASL-4 Deployment and Security Standards. We plan to add more information about what those entail in a future update.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those from the previous row, but to a higher standard—to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: Similar measures are required but at a higher standard resisting even well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen weights.

locator: Table 1 / Novel chem/bio weapons production / Mitigations-ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production; Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
excerpt: This would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4, but it depends on the capabilities of the strongest and most plausible threat actors that are not bound by a credible governance regime enforcing the recommendations for industry-wide safety outlined here.
paraphrase: The recommended security level is roughly RAND SL4, contingent on the capabilities of the strongest unregulated threat actors.

locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
excerpt: AI systems that are highly relied on and have extensive access to sensitive assets as well as moderate capacity for autonomous, goal-directed operation and subterfuge—such that it is plausible these AI systems could (if directed toward this goal, either deliberately or inadvertently) carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe.
paraphrase: This row's threshold is AI with high reliance, sensitive-asset access, and moderate autonomous/subterfuge capacity plausibly able to cause sabotage raising catastrophe odds.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: We expect to continue refining our framework in response to future risks (for example, the risk that an AI system attempts to subvert the goals of its operators).

locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
excerpt: In the near term, this possibility will likely be most applicable to AI systems that are extensively used within major AI companies, with the opportunity to manipulate how their successor systems are trained and deployed as well as the evidence used to assess their safety.
paraphrase: Near-term, this risk mainly applies to AI extensively used internally at major AI companies that could manipulate successor training or safety evidence.

locator: Table 1 / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities; Column: Capability or usage threshold
excerpt: Down the line, this possibility may come to apply to AI systems deployed within government and other high-stakes settings.
paraphrase: Longer-term, this risk may extend to AI deployed in government and other high-stakes contexts.
